title: So I'm trying to port New Super Mario Bros Wii on 3DS in Astra (because I love Mario and haven't played this yet) but was looking for advice to possibly speed up the process?
author: mattyjoe0706
selftext:
So I've been working on this for the past two days. It's taking a long time 1. Because I'm on plus so I can only do medium effort and limits run out fast but 2. For world 1 level 1 it is doing a test for terrain, model, so it's being thorough and doing quite well in it's thoroughness and accuracy it's just the slowness. 

Is there a way I could speed this up? It said after first level it won't do one at a time unless something new comes up which does happen a decent amount in Mario. Could use some advice here.

comments.author: UnderStrangeStars
comments.body:
You can speed it up, by spending a lot of money. If you want to do a major project within the confines of a prepaid subscription... everything worth doing will take weeks or months.

If you want it faster, you pay for more throughput. Even that will take time and iteration loops. The best AI projects I've seen, when talking to the prompters they describe 100s of prompts.

replies.author: mattyjoe0706
replies.body: I just don't know how people are doing these one shot things. Are they paying for plus and have access to higher effort levels?

comments.author: ThatOtherOneReddit
comments.body:
I've been doing a decomp project in Astra and been getting good results with emulator save states and logs. Essentially a lot of emulators let you add parallel tracing outputs to their jit compilation.

https://github.com/ChaseLewis/DolphinTASStudio

This enables an iterative feedback loop. It broke a problem if been trying to trying to solve in my favorite game after 72 hours of testing and iteration.

With enough save states and testing I'm convinced it should always be able to port / decomp a game assuming enough time and money.
